summary: Jira automation: SLA reminders + triage required-field validation + known-issues index prompt
description:
Goal: Reduce time-to-triage + prevent avoidable back-and-forth by enforcing minimum triage context and keeping SLA timers visible/acted on.

This ticket implements Jira Automation rules for the Customer Support project (SUP-*) and light-touch prompts to link customers/workflows to the Known Issues hub.

Scope
1) SLA reminders
- Automated reminders when first response or next update cadence is at-risk or breached.
- Reminders should be Support-friendly (actionable, not noisy) and aligned to the new SLA policy by tier.

2) Required field validation at triage
- When a SUP ticket transitions into Triage (or In Progress), validate a small set of required fields needed for effective escalation to SRE/Eng.
- If fields are missing, block progression (or immediately bounce back to New with a clear comment) and tag the reporter/assignee with what’s missing.

3) Known-issues index prompt (auto-link suggestion)
- When a SUP ticket matches common recurring categories (streaming disconnects, 429/quota confusion, autoscaling oscillation, private installer upgrade stuck, audit log lag), prompt the agent to check/link the Known Issues Index and applicable workaround article.
- This is a prompt only (no forced auto-resolution), to avoid misclassifying novel incidents.

Non-goals
- Changing Support SLA policy language (tracked elsewhere).
- Building new fields beyond what’s already in the guidelines (we should start with validation + reminders first).
acceptance_criteria:
SLA reminders
- A1: For SUP tickets in status New/Triage/In Progress (excluding Waiting on Customer/Resolved/Closed), post an internal comment and send a notification to #support-ops when first-response timer is within 15 minutes of due OR overdue.
- A2: For P0/P1 SUP tickets, send an additional reminder if no public update is logged within the expected cadence (per tier policy) after the last public update timestamp.
- A3: Reminders are de-duped (no more than 1 reminder per ticket per hour) to avoid alert fatigue.

Required field validation at triage
- B1: On transition to Triage, validate: customer tier, affected region(s), model (or endpoint type), impact summary, and at least one of (request IDs / timestamps window / reproduction steps).
- B2: If missing fields, automation posts a checklist-style comment with exactly what’s missing and how to get it (link to Support intake checklist).
- B3: If missing fields, ticket cannot move to In Progress (either block transition or auto-revert with comment).

Known-issues index prompt
- C1: When agent sets Component/Label consistent with a known-issue category OR sets priority P2+ with matching summary keywords, automation comments with: (1) link to Known Issues Index, (2) the most likely workaround article(s), and (3) reminder to add the KB link in the customer reply if applicable.
- C2: Prompt is suppressed for tickets labeled security-sensitive or customer-sensitive.

Operational
- D1: All rules have clear owner (Support Ops + Tooling) and are documented in the Jira field guidelines page.
- D2: Rollout starts with a 48-hour dry run (comment-only, no transition blocking) before enabling hard enforcement.
implementation_notes:
Proposed Jira Automation rules (draft)

Rule 1 — Triage required fields (dry run)
- Trigger: Issue transitioned -> To status = Triage
- Condition: Project = customer-support (SUP)
- Condition: Labels does not contain security-sensitive
- Action: IF any missing required fields THEN
  - Add internal comment:
    "Triage checklist missing: <fields>. Please update before moving forward. Intake checklist: <link>"
  - Add label: triage-missing-context
  - Notify channel: #support-ops (via Slack automation / email)
- No transition blocking in dry run mode.

Rule 2 — Triage required fields (enforcement)
- Same as Rule 1, but add action to revert status to New OR prevent transition to In Progress by reverting when status changes to In Progress and missing fields.
- Prefer pattern: allow transition to Triage but prevent transition to In Progress (less disruptive during initial intake).

Rule 3 — SLA first-response at-risk reminder
- Trigger: Scheduled (every 10 minutes)
- JQL (approx): project = SUP AND status in (New, Triage) AND "First Response Due" <= now() + 15m AND labels not in (sla-reminded)
- Action:
  - Internal comment: "First response due soon (<timestamp>). If awaiting customer info, set status=Waiting on Customer." 
  - Add label: sla-reminded
  - Send Slack notification to #support-ops with key + assignee + priority.
- De-dupe: set an entity property or label with timestamp (preferred) OR remove/expire label via a second scheduled rule after 60m.

Rule 4 — Update cadence reminder (P0/P1)
- Trigger: Scheduled (every 15 minutes)
- Condition: priority in (P0, P1) AND status in (Triage, In Progress) AND status != Waiting on Customer
- Condition: last public comment/customer update older than threshold (tier-aware)
- Action: comment + notify #support-ops

Rule 5 — Known-issues prompt
- Trigger: Field value changed (Component, Labels, Priority) OR Issue created
- If summary/labels/components match patterns:
  - streaming: "stream", "disconnect", "reset", "truncated"
  - quota: "429", "rate limit", "quota", "headers"
  - dedicated scaling: "autoscaling", "oscillation", "churn", "replicas"
  - private upgrade: "installer", "migrations", "upgrade stuck"
  - audit logs: "audit log", "delivery lag", "delayed"
- Action: internal comment with links:
  - Known issues index
  - Specific workaround page(s)
  - Reminder: "If this matches, paste workaround and include ‘when to escalate’ guidance."
- Suppress if labels include: security-sensitive, customer-sensitive, legal

Open questions
- Where is the canonical field for ‘public update timestamp’? If we don’t have one, we may need to start by using last customer-visible comment OR add a simple checkbox/field later.
- Tier-aware thresholds: do we encode tier table in automation (hardcoded) or use lookup via a Jira field (Customer Tier)? Start hardcoded for enterprise/dedicated/private/self_serve based on SLA policy page.

Dependencies
- INT-332: Slack automation for support bridges (channel + template). If Slack notification method changes, coordinate.
- Jira fields used must match the published guidelines page to avoid drift.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (today): Implement rules in disabled state, validate JQL matches ~expected volume using audit log.

Phase 1 (48h dry run): Enable Rule 1 (triage checklist comment only) + Rule 3 (first-response at-risk) as comment-only (no transitions). Monitor noise in #support-ops.

Phase 2 (enforce): Enable prevention/revert for missing triage fields when transitioning to In Progress.

Phase 3 (known-issues prompts): Enable Rule 5 and tune keyword/component matching based on false positives.

Phase 4 (update cadence): Enable P0/P1 update reminders once we confirm a reliable signal for public updates.
risks: Primary risk is notification fatigue (too many reminders) leading to ignored automation. Secondary risk is over-enforcement causing tickets to bounce during high-volume incidents. We mitigate via dry run, de-dupe, and narrowing enforcement to the In Progress transition.
comments: 2026-02-10 (Dev Patel): This is the #1 tooling gap coming out of the escalation playbook refresh. On-call asked for consistent context before pages; we can’t rely on training alone. Please start with dry-run comments so we can tune the required fields list.

2026-02-11 (Dylan Brooks): Drafted Rule 1 + Rule 3 in Jira Automation (disabled). Need confirmation on exact field names:
- Customer Tier (single select)
- Affected Region(s) (multi)
- Model / Endpoint (text vs select)
- Impact Summary (textarea)
- Request IDs (textarea)
If any of these don’t exist consistently, I’ll align to the Jira field guidelines page and update it with exact names.

2026-02-12 (Owen Phillips): +1 on blocking only at In Progress. During active incidents we triage quickly and fill fields while we investigate. If we block earlier, we’ll end up fighting the workflow. Required: region, model/endpoint, impact summary, and request IDs/timestamps window.

2026-02-13 (Rachel Kim): For enterprise accounts, make sure reminders don’t imply we owe 30-min updates 24/7. Language should reference coverage windows (business hours vs after-hours) and say “per tier policy”.

2026-02-14 (Dylan Brooks): Implemented dry-run required-fields comment. Added suppression for labels security-sensitive/customer-sensitive. Next: set up scheduled JQL for first-response ‘at risk’ reminders. Need a Slack destination: #support-ops vs #support. Preference?
2026-02-14 (Dev Patel): Use #support-ops for reminders. #support is too noisy and will get ignored. For P0/P1 only, also @mention on-call coordinator in the comment (we can manually tune later).

2026-02-15 (Chris Osei): Please add a lightweight metric: count of tickets hitting triage-missing-context label and median time from New -> Triage. We want to show impact in the post-sprint metrics review.

2026-02-16 (Dylan Brooks): Known-issues prompt rule draft is ready but I’m holding it until we confirm keyword mapping to avoid spamming. I’ll ship SLA first-response reminders + triage dry run first, then enable known-issues prompts with limited categories (streaming + 429) as a pilot.
